state.case_summary:
A 37-year-old woman with no past medical history presented with continuous chest pain for two hours. She denied dyspnea, syncope, or prior similar episodes. There was no personal or family history of cardiovascular or thromboembolic disease. Vital signs were: pulse 110/min, blood pressure 100/65 mmHg, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 37 °C, oxygen saturation 95% on room air (99% on 2 L/min nasal cannula). Cardiac auscultation was normal, and neck veins were not distended. Initial ECG showed sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3. She was given aspirin, clopidogrel, and intravenous heparin and taken to the catheterization laboratory. Twenty minutes later, a second ECG showed a new right bundle branch block and resolution of the precordial ST-segment elevations. Forty-five minutes after presentation, coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries without stenosis. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. pulmonary embolism
B. elevation of the ST segment is wide including conditions with secondary of the myocardium … pre existing ST elevation
C. Acute myocardial infarction
D. Preexisting ST elevation without acute ischemia
E. Myocarditis or pericarditis
F. Electrolyte imbalance
G. Rate
H. Aortic dissection

root.label: Acute Chest Pain Syndrome with Suspected Cardiac Aetiology and ECG Abnormality
supporting_facts: Continuous chest pain for two hours
ECG showed sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
Vital signs: pulse 110/min, blood pressure 100/65 mmHg, respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 95% on room air
excluded_candidates: Pulmonary embolism: not initially considered due to lack of dyspnea or syncope, but still a possible cause of chest pain and ECG changes
Myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries: possible due to coronary artery spasm or other mechanisms
alarm_features: ECG changes suggestive of cardiac ischemia
salient_findings: ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
Borderline hypotension with blood pressure 100/65 mmHg
Estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg
